title: Bootstrap Mapping for Object Storage And Tenant Prefixes And Signed Urls Semantic Contract
description: Canonical governance mapping from a semantic contract to future implementation target, provider/adapter target, expected tests, proof gates, deferrals, and blockers. It creates no runtime or scaffold files.
aiGuidance: Use this mapping as bootstrap planning authority only. Do not create implementation paths, claim production readiness, or start USF-39 from this record.

expectedTests.expectation: Future local dev tests use in-memory providers and deterministic synthetic fixtures; no in-memory provider satisfies test-compose proof.
Future test proof uses local Docker Compose OSS providers and deterministic synthetic data; no staging, production, or live provider claim is made.

expectedProofGates.expectation: Local dev proof may use in-memory or hermetic providers and must remain explicitly local/hermetic.
Test readiness requires local composed OSS providers for provider-backed claims.
Staging and live-external-provider proof remain outside this bootstrap scope and must not be inferred from local/test proof.
Production-live proof is not claimed by bootstrap mappings.

deferrals.reason: Staging, production, live-external-provider, production-live, and deployment proof are deferred from the first bootstrap readiness scope.
Implementation extraction remains blocked until USF-100 is signed and a separate USF-39 start action is authorised.

blockers.reason: Exact target files, per-slice topology, and per-slice source-use disposition must be reviewed before any implementation file is created.
blockers.blockingUntil: Signed USF-100 plus per-slice topology/source-use gate and clean validators.
